title: adaptive holdback + backpressure hull: reduce starvation in continuous-batcher
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: Continuous batching in high-concurrency tails occasionally starved small, latency-sensitive requests when large KV-heavy streams dominated the batch window. This PR introduces an adaptive holdback window plus a lightweight backpressure-hull admission policy to reduce starvation while preserving batch efficiency. Design summary: 1) adaptive_holdback: maintain a sliding holdback budget per worker based on observed per-client tail latency and recent admit/drop ratios; the budget reduces the effective batch window for new requests from noisy/kv-heavy flows so short requests can be admitted sooner; 2) backpressure_hull: a compact admission classifier that computes a 3-point hull (latency, kv_weight, size) to fast-reject requests that likely cause prolonged KV pinning and instead route them to a slightly slower lane (same model variant) that has prewarmed KV caches; 3) timeout_annealing: when a queue detects starvation for > SLO fraction, it anneals the per-slot timeout down for a bounded epoch to flush short requests; 4) kernel-hint passthrough: add a small runtime hint to kernel_selector to prefer the low-latency kernel path for requests admitted via the accelerated lane. The combined effect reduces p99 for short-requests by ~20% in local perf runs without materially increasing overall cost. The description below includes the checklist and testing notes. Checklist: - [x] API: add holdback config to ContinuousBatcher::Config - [x] Scheduler: implement adaptive_holdback and backpressure_hull admission paths - [x] Runtime: expose kernel_hint flag to kernel selector - [x] KV: add lightweight prewarm-lane tagging in cache manager - [x] Metrics: add holdback_budget, hull_rejects, anneal_epochs - [x] Tests: unit tests for admission, integration perf harness run - [x] Docs: short notes in docs/scheduling.md Rollout: feature-flagged (runtime flag continuous_adaptive_holdback) default off, enabled for Canary in DC-us-west-2. Migration notes: config defaults are conservative; operators can tune holdback.min_budget and anneal.window to trade throughput vs latency. See linked Linear tasks for tuning plans.
